page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with no margin notes. Running head at top centre. Page number at top left. Centred division heading "CAPITIS SECVNDI" with "versus I." beneath it. Italic verse quotation below. Catchword at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.p: 8. Qui in creaturis potius quàm in creatore confidunt, sibijpsis & aliis, maximo utrorumq; malo, imponunt. vers.8.
9. Per fidem & voto gratitudinis nos obstringimus, & idem illud exsoluimus. vers.9.
10. Fidelis est Deus, ut ait Apostolus, qui nō sinet uos tentari supra id quod potestis, sed præstabit unà cum tentatione etiam euasione, ut possitis sufferre. 1.Cor. 10.13. Joan.1.10.

11. Sicut Jonas post trinoctium in ven-tre ceti exactum, in lucem mirando mo-do prodijt, euomente eum ceto: ita Filius hominis Jesus Christus è corde terræ re-divivus prodijt, parta nobis non solum spirituali, sed etiam carnis nostræ resur-rectione.
main_text.head: CAPITIS SECVNDI versus I.

p.i: Et orauit Jonah ad Jehouam Deum su-um de ventre piscis.

main_text.p: In hoc loco occurrit exemplū illustre distorum [?] Prophetarum: Invoca me in die tribulationis, & eruam te, & glorifica bis me [?]: Pfal.50.15. Item: Jehouah in an-

page.notes: The catchword "gustia" is printed as "guftia", with long s rendered as plain s. The printed word "distorum" is uncertain (possibly "dictorum"), marked [?]. "bis me" in the Psalm quotation is uncertain, marked [?]. Several long s forms (e.g. "pofsitis", "euafione") are normalised to plain s as the rules require. The line "Item: Jehouah in an-" ends on a hyphen, and the rest of the word is the catchword below. The page has no marginal notes.
